The ITER and JT-60SA models answer the same question: what a set of converters does to the coils they drive, through windings, lines, grounding and the magnetic coupling between them. JT-60SA is where the method is checked against measured data, and ITER is where it is used. The two models should therefore share one foundation, so that what JT-60SA teaches transfers to ITER by construction rather than by re-implementation.

This plan builds that foundation: one set of composed classes, the same for both machines, in which every coil carries its distributed winding capacitance and every ITER supply, VS1 and its connection to PF2–PF5 included, is a circuit the model can predict. The physics stays where it is; what changes is that each concept has one owner.

§1 — Why one foundation

The two machines grew from parallel paths. The code at e2a75c81 shows where they diverge:

  • Three independent JT-60SA ten-coil lists: COILS in circuit.py, the same literal in current_identity.py, and _COILS in coil_system.py.
  • A passive-structure record that cannot hold unlabelled filaments: nova_plant.averaged_plant fabricates alternating vessel and cryostat labels to satisfy PassiveStructure's group rule.
  • Two firing gate windows and two bridge stamps: JT60SAFiring.gate keeps its own window beside FiringGenerator.gate, and _stamp_jt60sa_bridge re-stamps the bridge add_unit builds.
  • Coil construction decided by name: coil_windings.py branches on geometry.name.startswith("CS"), "PF" or "VS" in five places, keys PF_DOUBLE_PANCAKES by ITER name and TERMINAL_UNIT_LAYERS by the first two letters. A JT-60SA coil therefore cannot reach the turn-resolved path except by being renamed.

Machine assembly also lives in the study scripts rather than the library. scripts/iter/pf_switched_pulse.py is 1,656 lines and builds its own windings and stress measures. scripts/iter/initiation_transient.py builds its own coil models. So each new study re-assembles the machine.

The most consequential gap is capacitance. ITER's sectioned windings carry geometry-computed distributed capacitance (winding strays), and their first PF modes fall at 260–690 Hz, inside the converter band. JT-60SA has the same sectioned-winding code with its own pancake layouts (JT-60SA windings), but the coupled plant scored against the measured coil-to-coil coupling is R–L with nova's mutuals and passive structure only. JT-60SA's 6f, 12f and 18f lines (about 365, 730 and 1,095 Hz) sit just below its ideal winding modes (868 Hz–2.43 kHz). The measured coupling rises with frequency where nova's stays flat (jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §14). The distributed winding is the one capacitive form not yet scored against that data, and the test needs both machines' coils built the same way.

§2 — The shared component classes

No new vocabulary. Every concept below already has an owner, and the shared model is those owners, extended so that both machines build from them and composed rather than inherited. Machine-specific numbers come from records: the IDS machine description, the IDM register (IDM register) and the JT-60SA sources register. They never come from name prefixes or module constants. The owner of each concept:

  • Plant: nova_plant.NovaPlant, nova's coupled coils, passive structure and prescribed plasma. It holds one PassiveStructure record. That record gains a way to carry unlabelled filaments, so averaged_plant stops inventing labels. §3 adds the section-resolved ports here.
  • Forms: the existing entry points derive each form from the one composition. These are nova_plant.averaged_plant for the averaged state space, nova_plant.into_switched for the switched multiport that switched_circuit.Circuit integrates, and coil_coupling.terminal_impedance and sectioned_response for the analytic frequency domain. There is no new forms module, so the forms cannot drift apart.
  • Circuit: circuit_connections.CircuitConnections, which already holds a circuit's branches and incidence, extended to hold its supply, coils, lines and grounding. filter_network.BoosterLoop is today's JT-60SA-only composition of converter filter, coil, grounding and mutual. It becomes one instance of the circuit and retires as a class.
  • Supply and its units: supply.SupplyModel and supply.SeriesUnit, the existing per-unit converter composition with firing phase and thyristor phasors, imported by 25 files. A SeriesUnit gains its firing law as a strategy, its protection and, where fitted, its switching network or discharge unit. The ITER thyristor law, the CS circulating law, the JT-60SA booster law and the IGBT modulator implement one interface, converter_units.FiringGenerator's, so the gate window exists once. converter_units.ConverterNetwork stamps any unit into the switched netlist.
  • Winding: coil_windings.WindingGeometry and SectionedWinding, with TurnInsulation. WindingGeometry gains each coil's manufactured layout as a record (pancakes, layers, turns, hands), so construction never reads a coil's name. The distributed capacitance, turn to turn, section to section and section to ground, stays with coil_coupling's capacitance_nodal, capacitive_ladder and sectioned_response. A separate coil class is added only if SectionedWinding cannot carry a coil's terminals and feeder; the node that adds it says why.
  • Line: busbar_lines. Its module functions become a frozen Line dataclass with those functions as methods: distributed resistance, inductance and capacitance per unit length, in segments. The ITER DC busbars, the VS1 connection to PF2–PF5 and the JT-60SA feeders are all Lines. This is the one new class, and it replaces functions rather than adding surface beside them.
  • Grounding: filter_network.GroundingSystem, extended to carry ITER's grounding as well as JT-60SA's.

The section's public surface shrinks overall:

  • BoosterLoop retires into the circuit;
  • the JT-60SA firing class and bridge stamp merge into the shared strategy and stamp;
  • the duplicate coil lists go;
  • the busbar_lines functions become one class's methods.

Done when:

  • An ITER coil (PF6) and a JT-60SA coil (EF4) are built through the same WindingGeometry and SectionedWinding owners from their machine descriptions and layout records, in one test.
  • Each divergence in §1 is removed. The deleted code is shown, and a test reaches the single owner that remains: one coil list for each machine, a passive-structure record that holds unlabelled filaments, one gate window, one bridge stamp, one circuit composition with BoosterLoop retired, and construction from layout records, never from names.
  • Behaviour is unchanged. The whole suite passes with the same count. The frozen dummy-load prediction JSON stays byte-identical, and tests/test_claims_register.py passes.
  • Negative control: a coil with no layout record raises an error naming the coil, instead of being modelled as a two-layer double pancake.

§3 — Distributed capacitance in both machines' plants

Every coil in the ITER and JT-60SA coupled plants carries its Winding's distributed capacitance. Its section mutuals come from nova's finite rectangular kernels, one thick element per section, as the flux maps now use for whole coils. The plant exports section-resolved ports, so a study reads internal voltages as well as terminals. The ports extend NovaPlant. The per-study coupling of windings into a plant, coil_windings.add_coupled_windings and add_prescribed_winding_sources, retires into them.

Where the insulation is undocumented, the capacitance carries a stated range and every result is reported at both ends. JT-60SA's turn, pancake and ground layers have no thickness or permittivity in the held sources, so its range is the replay windings record's.

Done when:

  • For each ITER PF coil, the converged isolated winding's first mode reproduces its turn-resolved reference within 1 %, under the same terminal boundary condition and loss assumptions. No turn-resolved reference exists for the CS modules, whose held record is a seven-section equal split, so for each CS module the measure is convergence: halving every section's length moves the first mode by less than 1 %. The full coupled plant's first terminal-impedance peak, and its shift from that isolated reference, are reported at both installed-loss bounds without the 1 % limit: mutual coupling to the other coils, the plant's resistance and the converter move it physically, so the shift is a result, not a convergence error. The PF reference is PF frequency response, and the CS reference is winding strays. The two VS coils keep one electrical section each, because their internal layout is not published. The record says so and lists the missing layout.
  • For each JT-60SA EF and CS coil, the first mode is reported at both ends of the insulation range. The nominal case reproduces the replay windings record's 868 Hz–2.43 kHz span.
  • Positive control: with every capacitance set to zero, the plant reproduces today's R–L plant to 0.1 %. That means the JT-60SA harmonic transfer functions at 6f, 12f and 18f, and ITER's nova-plant terminal impedance.
  • Negative control: with losses removed, doubling every capacitance of one coil lowers each of its modes by a factor of √2, within 0.1 %.
  • Section transients converge: with the installed damping carried, halving the switched step moves no section voltage peak or section dv/dt by more than 1 %. The first integrated run, without damped sections, saw settled section peaks shift by up to 1,743 % when its step was halved.

§4 — Every ITER supply as a composed circuit, the VS1 line included

The thirteen ITER supplies the integrated model drives are each built as one Circuit from the IDM register: CS1 (CS1U and CS1L in series), CS2U, CS2L, CS3U, CS3L, PF1 to PF6, VS1 and VS3. No value is taken from DINA, which is the demand, not the design. The correction-coil and TF supplies, which decision iter-coverage adds, are §7's.

VS1 is modelled whole: its thyristor pair and four IGBT units, and its Line to the PF2–PF5 connection points. That Line is distributed, with inductance and capacitance from the register or, where IDM is silent, from a stated assumption added to the register.

The circuits are data, not code. One factory builds any circuit from its register entries, so this section adds one public function and one refusal: the refusal of a parameter that has no source. That refusal is the design-authority rule enforced in code, and no existing refusal covers it.

For each circuit the model predicts two things:

  • the frequency response: the terminal impedance, and the transfer from each converter line to every terminal and section voltage, to ground and across;
  • the switched response over a chosen window.

Done when:

  • All thirteen circuits build from the register. A test refuses a circuit with any parameter that has neither a register citation nor a stated assumption.
  • Each circuit, run through the composed model instead of its study's own assembly, reproduces the numbers the merged studies pinned in the claims register. A pin with a band is reproduced within it. A pin recorded without a band, such as VS1's sampled loop at 6.04 dB and 61.03° at 71.35 Hz, is reproduced to 1 % of its pinned value, because the composed circuit carries the same arithmetic. Other examples are the PF2/PF5 line gains and the initiation peaks.
  • The VS1 Line's first resonance and the PF2–PF5 connection-point voltage response are reported, with the line's capacitance at both ends of its range.
  • Negative control: opening VS1's galvanic connection reduces PF2's and PF5's response to VS1's carrier to the mutual-inductance coupling alone, as nova's mutual predicts.
  • The switched response runs on the large plants. Under decision large-plant-propagator (revised 19 October), the composed VS1 circuit runs on the companion integrator with its port factor cache. The cache took a 1 ms VS1 window from 489 s to 34.8 s with the same switching events. Its accuracy is shown by step halving: halving the step moves no terminal, connection-point or first-turn peak by more than 1 %. Under the lead's decision long-window-modelling (iter-switched-terminal-transients), the 120 ms PF2 windows run on the terminal plant through the exact modal path. The sectioned plant runs on short windows around switching events, started from the long run's state at that instant. The exact modal path keeps its energy balance, closed within 1e-6 where it runs. Negative control: doubling the companion step on VS1 moves a peak by more than the halving does, so the step-halving check has resolution.

The claims-register pins that need every supply switching together on one plant are measured by iter-switched-terminal-transients §6, which assembles that run. They are the whole-pulse replay pins, the integrated insertion pins and the sampled loop margins. This section closes on the pins one composed circuit can reproduce, the VS1 line's response, and VS1's first-turn step criterion. The averaged plant adapter's positive-energy refusal of the cached plant is diagnosed here, because the composed circuits' averaged response needs it. Moving these pins removes a circular wait: §6 needed this section closed, and these pins needed §6's assembly.

§5 — JT-60SA's circuits on the same classes

EF1–EF6 and CS1–CS4 are built through the same owners: CircuitConnections, SupplyModel and SeriesUnit, SectionedWinding, Line and GroundingSystem. Each carries the following:

  • the base supply, booster or switching unit, and quench-protection circuit tabulated in jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §2;
  • the 2023 filter and the as-built grounding from jt60sa-power-supply-sources §3.

The booster is composed from its documented bridges (jt60sa-power-supply-sources §2) at design values. The fitted booster model the coil-circuit plan's integrated run needs stays held by that plan's gate g-jccm-1.

Done when:

  • With capacitance off, the composed JT-60SA plant reproduces the stored results unchanged: the coil-to-coil transfer functions of jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §5 (eight of nine pairs within 4–8 % of M/L) and the 45 judged slow-current windows of §7.
  • With capacitance on, the same runs are reported beside them.
  • Negative control: exchanging two coils' layout records changes both coils' modes, and the test that pins them fails.

§6 — The studies call the shared model

The machine assembly inside the study scripts is replaced by calls to the composed model. That covers scripts/iter/pf_switched_pulse.py, initiation_transient.py, current_controllers.py, dummy_load_prediction.py and, once it lands, integrated_simulation.py, plus the JT-60SA replay and plant scripts. Each script keeps its command line and its outputs.

This section runs last. It follows §9, which gives the plant one owner, and the first stage of iter-switched-terminal-transients §6, so it does not refactor scripts that run imports. Every study, integrated_model.py included, then reads the plant from §9's owner, and the re-export §9 leaves in current_controllers.py is removed.

Done when:

  • No study script defines a coil, winding, converter unit, line or passive structure of its own. An import-graph test checks this.
  • tests/test_claims_register.py passes, the frozen dummy-load JSON stays byte-identical, and the whole suite passes with the same count.
  • Each script's line count is reported before and after.
  • No study script, and no src module other than nova_plant.py, names a plant cache path. The import-graph test checks this and covers integrated_model.py.
  • Negative control: a local winding definition added to a scratch copy of one script fails the import-graph test.

§7 — The correction-coil supplies

Decision iter-coverage extends the model to every ITER coil supply. This section builds the correction-coil supplies through the owners §2 extends and the circuit factory §4 adds; §8 builds the TF supply. Their IDM values were looked up by the coordinator on 17 October 2026, and a node enters them in the IDM register with their citations.

  • Correction coils: nine independent circuits, three each at the top, side and bottom. Each feeds a pair of diametrically opposite coils in series and anti-series. Each converter is a 12-pulse, four-quadrant thyristor converter of four six-pulse bridges, rated ±10 kA. The on-load output is ±85 V for the top and bottom circuits and ±300 V for the side circuits (SRD-41, 28B6XQ v6.0, Table 2.2.6; Q3ZSRQ v1.1). There is no separate discharge unit: the converters discharge the coils, and on a converter fault the circuit resistance must give L/R ≤ 18 s (28B6XQ v6.0 §2.2.3.4.2). Each coil is 9–10 mH, and the terminal voltage to ground is at most 110 V (top and bottom) and 300 V (side) in operation (A7BSV3 v1.1, revision required).

IDM is silent on the correction-coil busbar and feeder inductance and resistance. Those enter the register as stated assumptions. None is taken from DINA.

The correction coils are not axisymmetric. In nova's axisymmetric plant, an anti-series pair links no net flux with the PF and CS coils. Their circuits therefore couple to the plant only through ground, a stated assumption the record carries.

Done when:

  • All nine correction-coil circuits build from the register through the same factory as §4's, and the factory refuses any parameter with no source.
  • For each circuit, the model predicts the frequency response (terminal impedance, and the transfer from each converter line to the coil terminals, to ground and across) and the switched response over one current ramp.
  • Each correction-coil circuit's fault decay meets L/R ≤ 18 s, or the record names by how much it misses.
  • Negative control: connecting one correction-coil pair in series rather than anti-series gives it a non-zero net mutual with PF6, so the axisymmetric decoupling the record assumes is a property of the anti-series connection and not of the code.

§8 — The TF supply

One 12-pulse, two-quadrant thyristor converter rated 68 kA drives the eighteen TF coils in series. Each coil's self-inductance is 349 mH; with the mutual coupling between the TF coils, the series string is 17.7 H, not 18 × 0.349 = 6.28 H. Both are SRD values, carried in the register as stated assumptions until their IDM page is located. Nine fast-discharge units sit between the nine coil pairs, and the SRD gives an equivalent L/R of 11 s (28B6XQ v6.0 §2.2.3.1). The converter gives ±160 V in normal operation and ±650 V for charge and discharge (Q69TXL v2.2 PDF 11, 27–28). §8's remaining work, the switched response over one current ramp, runs after §4's VS1 window, on the same companion integrator; §7 does not wait on it. The IDM register gives the TF voltage to ground as 1.0 kV nominal, 7.0 kV in fast discharge and 15.0 kV in a fault (22HLVN v1.0, Table 4). The circuit is built through the owners §2 extends and the factory §4 adds.

The coordinator settled the discharge configuration from 778SPD v1.0 on 18 October 2026.

  • Arrangement: nine fast-discharge units are interleaved in series with the nine coil pairs (p. 8). Each unit therefore sees one resistor's voltage, and the interleaving keeps the voltage to ground limited.
  • Resistance: each resistor is 0.111 Ω at 20 °C, 0.999 Ω for all nine (pp. 29, 33).
  • Peak voltage per unit: 7.5 kV at 20 °C without transients; 8.5 kV including the main-breaker transient; 10 kV including the pyrobreaker transient (pp. 10, 29).
  • Heating: a discharge starting at 20 °C ends at 236 °C, with the resistance risen by a factor of 2.34 (p. 29). The end temperature must not exceed 300 °C.

Each fast-discharge unit links one pair of TF coils, and its discharge depends on the resistor's temperature. The lead confirmed both on 18 October 2026. With the coils' 17.7 H, the 11 s equivalent time constant implies an equivalent resistance of about 1.61 Ω. That value lies between the resistors' initial 0.999 Ω and their final 2.34 × 0.999 ≈ 2.34 Ω at 236 °C. So the resistor heating accounts for the 11 s, with no missing inductance.

The method comes from the partner repository ~/Code/mctb, its fast-discharge model of the TF cold tests (docs/research/mctb-discharge-fit.html). That model has three parts, and it reproduces all ten TF17 and TF07 discharges to 0.04–0.27 % rms:

  • one inductance;
  • a dump-resistor law RF = RF0 + kFE, linear in the absorbed energy and adiabatic during a discharge, with AISI 304's temperature coefficient;
  • one passive coupled mode in each coil, with k² = 0.80 and τ₂ = 0.49 s, which drops the current by 0.68 % within half a second.

What transfers to the operational circuit is the method and the coil's passive mode, because TF17 and TF07 are ITER TF coils. What does not transfer is the cold-test resistor: a dedicated 5.5 mΩ unit discharging one coil with τ ≈ 60 s. The operational resistor law is set from 778SPD instead: 0.111 Ω at 20 °C, rising 2.34 times by the end of a discharge, at 236 °C.

Done when:

  • The TF circuit builds from the register through §4's factory, with the nine interleaved units, 0.111 Ω each, cited to 778SPD.
  • The model predicts the TF terminal impedance, the converter-line transfer to the coil terminals, to ground and across, and the switched response over one current ramp.
  • Each unit's resistor follows the energy law above, with RF0 = 0.111 Ω at 20 °C and kF set so the resistance reaches 2.34 times its initial value at the energy one unit absorbs in a full 68 kA discharge. Each coil carries the passive mode measured on TF17 and TF07. The discharge reproduces 778SPD's 11 s equivalent time constant within 5 %, with τ taken as 778SPD defines it: the current-squared equivalent τeq = 2∫I²dt / I0², which equals L/R for a constant resistance (778SPD v1.0 pp. 10, 29). The record also reports mctb's measure, a single exponential fitted from 80 % to 10 % of the starting current, and states why the two differ: the energy-linear resistor makes the decay non-exponential. Beside it, the record gives the constant-resistance decays at 0.999 Ω (about 17.7 s) and at 2.34 Ω (about 7.6 s), which bracket the result.
  • The peak voltage across each unit stays within 7.5 kV without transients, and within 8.5 kV and 10 kV with the breaker transients the model carries. Any excess is named.
  • Negative control: with the discharge units bypassed, the current decays only through the converter and the coil resistance, with a time constant at least ten times longer than 11 s. That shows the gate measures the discharge units and not the converter.

§9 — One plant owner, on a jointly passive plant

The coupled ITER plant every study reads is pinned in one constant, NOVA_PLANT_CACHE, defined in scripts/iter/current_controllers.py and imported by about a dozen scripts. That plant (key 28148563521d92a2198b) does not store positive energy. Its joint coil and passive linkage has two negative directions, VSU −3.84×10−8 H and VSL −3.25×10−8 H, from the eight VS3 steel jackets (§4, 9c654e94). On it, the analytic arm of iter-switched-terminal-transients §6 grows, and its energy account closes only to 5.2 %. A cold build does not repair it, because nova's linkage code is unchanged. The repair is nova's iter-passive-plasma-circuit §7, which issues a new 105069/3 plant entry and key.

This section moves the plant source into src/power_convertor/nova_plant.py, re-exports it as current_controllers.NOVA_PLANT_CACHE so every existing importer follows, and adopts nova's new key there. It is held until nova's §7 lands, and it runs before the first stage of iter-switched-terminal-transients §6 resumes.

Done when:

  • nova_plant.py is the one place that names the plant entry, and current_controllers.NOVA_PLANT_CACHE is read from it.
  • On the adopted plant, the joint coil and passive linkage S = L − MTM has no negative eigenvalue, every coil's bare inductance is positive, and the averaged linearised spectrum of the thirteen composed supplies has no positive rate. Negative control: the old pinned plant fails the same assertions.
  • Every composed-circuit pin measured on the old plant is measured again on the new one, and the record lists each with its move. A move beyond 1 % is reported with its cause and never fitted.

§10 — The switched path takes the full plasma source

plasma_input_matrix(plant) in nova_plant.py gives the switched path a plasma input on the coil ports only: −pinv(Lc), with zeros on every passive mode. into_switched feeds plant.plasma_rate, one column per coil, through it. A disruption drives every circuit, the passive structure included, so coil-supply-report-rebuild §6, a fast-discharge trip followed by a disruption, needs the plasma flux on every coil and passive mode. current_control.coupled_plant closed the same gap behind a full_source option (846ac2e3). This section adds that option to the switched path as an opt-in. It runs on §9's plant, because −L−1 through today's indefinite joint linkage would grow.

Done when:

  • into_switched(..., full_source=True) takes a plasma flux rate on every coil and passive mode, with the input −L−1 through the joint coil and passive linkage.
  • With the option off, the input matrix is unchanged bit for bit and the existing switched tests pass unchanged.
  • Positive control: a flux step on the passive modes alone moves the coil currents through the mutuals, as an analytic two-circuit case predicts.
  • Negative control: with the coil-to-passive mutual removed, the same step leaves the coil currents unmoved, so the test measures the coupling.

§ Decisions

Which ITER supplies does the shared model cover?

The lead asked on 17 October 2026 for models that predict the response of all ITER power converters and their coils, the VS1 line included. §4 builds the thirteen supplies the integrated run and the presentation results rest on. §7 builds the correction-coil supplies and §8 the TF supply, both after §4 because they call its circuit factory, and both from IDM values. None of their values is taken from DINA.

How the exact integrator propagates the large plants

<p>The exact integrator forms a dense modal basis for every new switch state. On the 2,881-state composed VS1 circuit and the 120 ms PF2 windows, node <code>exact-integrator-vs1-speed-2</code> profiled that per-state decomposition as the binding cost, not gate callbacks or caching. Its measurements show a rank-one modal update would not close the gap.</p>

Revised 19 October after node exact-integrator-vs1-speed-2 measured the Krylov action. Substepped, it converges to itself (2e-6 to 1e-5) but sits 1.05e-4 from the modal eigenbasis it would be gated against, and no exact-path operator fits a 1 ms VS1 window inside 570 s (modal about 1,700 s, dense Krylov about 980 s). The same node's port factor cache takes the companion integrator's 1 ms VS1 window from 489 s to 34.8 s with the same switching events. VS1 windows therefore run on the cached companion integrator, with step halving as the accuracy evidence, and the Krylov path is not pursued further. A matrix-free backward-Euler operator is recorded in the node's evidence as the route if it is ever needed. Small circuits keep the exact modal path and its energy balance.

Which DC busbar route length does the register carry for the PF/CS feeders the composed circuits are built on?

IDM prints no per-circuit route length. The only IDM-derived figure is 22HXXE's busbar leakage bound, which implies 170–480 m of busbar per circuit (5×10⁻⁷ S/m against 4.2–12 kΩ). 170 m is a lower bound, because that leakage figure is pessimistic. The 30 m assumption sat below the only IDM-derived figure, and it smoothed away the coil-end reflection the insertion pins rest on: PF1's 1 µs across-gain is 1.267 at 30 m, 1.373 at 170 m and 1.555 at 480 m. The register carries the range as a stated assumption, and the composed insertion runs at both ends, so its results are a band.

How does §4 settle VS1's step criterion, now that the whole 4 ms window does not converge at 0.125 µs?

At 0.125 µs only PF3's first turn converges. The connection points and terminal reverse because the 2.7–5.4 MHz line ring is under-resolved, and each full-window halving costs about four times the last, so brute force to about 0.01 µs is out of reach. Each peak is formed by one switching event. So step-halve a short window around each peak down to about 0.01 µs, with every arm started from one exact state at a shared grid instant. The full 4 ms window stays the stability evidence.

§ Followups

Build the shared classes first; this consolidation leads the project's work

The lead set this consolidation as the first priority on 17 October 2026. The order is §2, then §3. §4 and §5 follow §3 in parallel, because they write different circuits, and §6 comes last.

§2 runs as two nodes. The first takes the windings, coils and plant: coil_windings, coil_coupling, passive_structure, coupled_circuit, nova_plant and circuit. No live node writes those, so it starts at once. The second takes the converters, firing laws and lines: converter_units, bridge, commutation and busbar_lines. It starts when the transients stray sweep releases those paths. That sweep and the integrated-run assembly finish on today's code, and §6 here then moves them onto the shared model.

jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §16 waits on §3 through its gate.

/reckon-build shared-coil-supply-model §2

§2's first node landed (merged at 84ebf330; whole suite 1053 passed, 7 skipped of 1060), and its second is in review. §3's first attempt showed the section is several fences of work, so it is split. Superseded by f-scsm-002, which carries the order with §7 placed.

Build §3 as four nodes, then §4 and §5 in parallel, §7 after §4, and §6 last

§3 runs as four nodes in order:

  1. the finite-kernel section matrices for every ITER PF and CS coil;
  2. section ports on NovaPlant built from those matrices;
  3. the four quantitative gates as evidence;
  4. retiring add_coupled_windings and add_prescribed_winding_sources onto the ports, and carrying the damping.

§4 and §5 follow §3 in parallel, because they write different circuits. §7 follows §4, because it calls §4's circuit factory. jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §16 waits on §3 through its gate. §6 comes last, and moves the parked integrated run onto the shared model.

/reckon-build shared-coil-supply-model §3

§4: compose VS3 as one anti-series coil pair, not two independent branches (low priority)

The register builds VS3 as two independent converter-to-coil loops (circuit_connections.topology “independent”, merged at ea8cc214). EFXUVH v2.1 gives one coil circuit instead: VS3U and VS3L “connected in an anti-series ‘saddle’ arrangement” (PDF 11, 111), with two converters in push-pull “connected to the 4-terminal VS3 coil circuit” that “shall always be operated in unison” (PDF 64); converter 1 is associated with VS3U and converter 2 with VS3L (PDF 88). The lead confirmed on 19 October 2026 that the loops are not independent. The register's “each branch two 1.2 kV cells” double-counts: the two cells are the two converters.

Recompose VS3 through the existing anti_series topology with the two converters in series, each one 1.2 kV-link H-bridge, and replace the independence assertions in tests/test_circuit_factory.py, tests/test_vs1_composed.py and tests/test_converter_units.py. How the windings are damped (lead direction, 18 October 2026). The model's damping is the best data-augmented estimate, not a first-principles one alone. A Q, or a loss scale, may enter the model, but only with a prior: a value, an interval and a source. The physical loss model supplies the prior: the earth unit, the ground screen, the dielectric and the conductor coupling, cited per mechanism in winding_losses.WindingLosses. Data update it:

  • JT-60SA's measured coil-to-coil transfer functions near the winding modes (jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §16 fits an installed-damping interval);
  • the PF dummy-load recordings;
  • any stored-coil frequency sweep, which counts only as a calibration of the cold state.

Numerical damping with no prior, placed only to make a solver converge, stays ruled out. The calibration acts as scale factors on the physical mechanisms, each with its prior interval, plus at most one residual modal-Q term with its own prior for losses the mechanisms do not carry. Code refuses a bare Q, as the circuit factory refuses an unsourced parameter. Every result reports the prior, the updated value and how far the data moved it.

The review of run r-20261020T135901124052-averaged-plant-energy-refusal at head 9c654e94f225d8b5d9ffa002d6f89e9bc6410615 parsed six dimensions (goal_fidelity 19, evidence 18, scope_discipline 18, durability 18, fit 18, reuse 20), added_failure_count 0, one follow-on finding. The node's diagnosis branch is sound: the averaged adapter correctly refuses a genuinely indefinite cached linkage, the guard is intact, and the three added refusal tests redden under its mutation.

<p>The cached plant is genuinely indefinite: Schur minimum −3.8377767548e-8 H, dominated by VSU, with a second VSL negative direction; the eight steel-jacket rows isolate the over-screening. The averaged guard remains intact, both sampled-loop pins are unmeasured, three new refusal cases fail when the guard is mutated, and base/head gates give 85/88 passed with zero added failures. <a href="/power_convertor/evidence/fragments/shared-coil-supply-model/averaged-plant-energy-refusal.html#averaged-plant-energy-refusal">Evidence and upstream cache repair</a>.</p>

The averaged adapter's refusal is correct: the cached nova plant is genuinely indefinite (merged 9c654e94; independent review 19/18/18/18/18/20, zero added failures). Its coil Schur complement has two negative eigenvalues, −3.84×10⁻⁸ H (almost entirely VSU) and −3.25×10⁻⁸ H (VSL). The eight steel jackets around the VS3 coils screen more flux than the coils link.

The cause lies upstream in nova's ITER machine description. Each VS3 conductor annulus is a 27.556 mm square, and its concentric steel jacket a 22.974 mm square at the same centre, so the jacket lies inside the conductor it surrounds. nova's raw passive block has 37 negative eigenvalues (minimum −2.53×10⁻⁷ H). Its stored, positive-definite-guarded copy is positive, but the joint coil and passive linkage is not. The cache holds 1,312 passive rows, where today's source recipe yields 2,186, so the recipe that built it is also unknown.

The guard stays. VS1's sampled-loop pin and VS3's margin pin stay unmeasured until nova supplies a jointly passive plant, and that request goes to the nova owner through the lead. Until then, any study using the cached plant on the VS3 coils carries this caveat.
